protocol.name: treeland_remote_subsurface_unstable_v1
protocol.copyright: SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 UnionTech Software Technology Co., Ltd. SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
protocol.description:
This protocol provides sub-surface relationships between wl_surface objects using token-based identifiers exchanged out-of-band, instead of the direct wl_surface references required by wl_subcompositor. This allows parent-child relationships both across different client connections and within the same client.
In wl_subcompositor both the parent surface and sibling surfaces must be local wl_surface objects from the same client. This protocol removes that restriction by using token-based identifiers exchanged out-of-band:
1. A client exports a wl_surface and receives a surface_token.
2. Another client (or the same client) exports their own wl_surface and then calls create_remote_subsurface with the parent's surface_token, attaching their surface as a child.
All sub-surface semantics follow the wl_subcompositor specification unless explicitly noted in this document. Cross-process sub-surfaces are always in desynchronized mode; synchronized mode is not supported.
This protocol is not interoperable with wl_subsurface: a treeland_remote_subsurface_v1 cannot be stacked relative to wl_subsurface siblings, and a wl_subsurface cannot reference a surface that carries a treeland_remote_subsurface_v1 role.
Clients should prefer this protocol over wl_subsurface for all sub-surface use, to avoid having two separate sub-surface trees that cannot interact with each other.
The compositor must restrict binding to trusted clients. A client that obtains a surface_token must only share it with other trusted clients through a secure mechanism; the compositor does not disclose tokens to other clients.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development. It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways, without incrementing the interface major version and without prior notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or semantics remaining stable across releases.

interface.name: treeland_remote_subsurface_manager_v1
interface.description:
Global factory for exporting wl_surface objects as token-addressable sub-surface parents or children.
The typical workflow is:
1. The client calls export_surface on a wl_surface to obtain a treeland_exported_surface_v1 and receive a surface_token event.
2. The token is shared out-of-band with another client.
3. That client exports its own wl_surface, then calls create_remote_subsurface with the parent's token to establish a sub-surface relationship.
Destroying this manager does not affect already-exported surfaces or existing sub-surface relationships; it only prevents creation of new exported surfaces.

entry.name: bad_surface
entry.summary: the wl_surface has already been exported through this manager

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys this manager object. Already-exported treeland_exported_surface_v1 objects and existing sub-surface relationships are not affected.

request.name: export_surface

description.summary: register a surface for token-addressable sub-surface use

request.description:
Registers a wl_surface as addressable by token, creating a treeland_exported_surface_v1. Upon success the compositor emits the surface_token event on the new object.
The surface must not have been previously exported through this manager; doing so is a bad_surface error. A surface may carry both an xdg_toplevel (or any other role) and an export; the export only marks it as addressable by token.

interface.name: treeland_exported_surface_v1

description.summary: an exported surface, addressable by token

interface.description:
Represents a wl_surface registered for sub-surface use via this protocol. The surface may act as a parent or a child; a surface can have at most one parent via this protocol.
Destroying this object revokes the surface_token without affecting existing parent-child relationships or treeland_remote_subsurface_v1 objects.

enum.name: error
enum.description: These errors can be raised in response to treeland_exported_surface_v1 requests.

entry.name: bad_surface
entry.summary: the child surface already has an incompatible role

enum.name: reject_reason
enum.description: Indicates why a create_remote_subsurface request could not establish the requested parent-child relationship.

entry.name: invalid_token
entry.summary: parent_token does not identify a live exported surface

entry.name: cyclic
entry.summary: parent_token would introduce a cycle in the sub-surface tree

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Revokes the surface_token; subsequent use of the token in create_remote_subsurface results in an invalid_token parent_rejected event on the requesting treeland_exported_surface_v1.
The client must destroy this object before destroying the associated wl_surface.

request.name: create_remote_subsurface

description.summary: attach this surface as a child to a remote parent

request.description:
Attaches the exported surface to the parent identified by parent_token, creating a treeland_remote_subsurface_v1. The surface must not already have a wlroots role; it will be assigned the exclusive treeland_remote_subsurface_v1 role. If the surface already has an incompatible role, a bad_surface error is raised and the new treeland_remote_subsurface_v1 object is inert.
If the parent_token is invalid or would introduce a cycle, the request is ignored and a parent_rejected event is emitted carrying the reject_reason.
The sub-surface addition is double-buffered on the parent.

arg.name: parent_token
arg.summary: surface_token of the parent, obtained via export

event.name: surface_token
event.description: Emitted immediately after export_surface. The token is a unique string of at most 128 characters, generated by a cryptographically secure random number generator, intended to be shared out-of-band so that other clients can reference this surface as a parent or sibling.

event.name: parent_rejected

description.summary: create_remote_subsurface could not attach to the parent

event.description: Emitted when create_remote_subsurface cannot establish the requested parent-child relationship.

interface.name: treeland_remote_subsurface_v1

description.summary: remote sub-surface interface to a wl_surface

interface.description:
An additional interface to a wl_surface that has been made a sub-surface via this protocol. A sub-surface has one parent and is not automatically clipped to its parent's area.
Mapping and commit semantics follow wl_subcompositor except that desynchronized mode is always used. A sub-surface never has the keyboard focus of any seat.
The parent is identified at creation time and cannot be changed. place_above and place_below accept a token (string) instead of a wl_surface proxy; see the request documentation for valid values.
The wl_surface.offset request is ignored; clients must use set_position instead.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Removes the sub-surface association, unmaps the wl_surface immediately, and destroys this object.

request.name: set_position
request.description: Schedules a position change relative to the parent surface coordinate system. Coordinates are not restricted to the parent area; negative values are allowed. Double-buffered on the parent; replaces any previous pending position. Initial position is 0, 0.

arg.name: x
arg.summary: x coordinate in the parent surface local coordinate system

arg.name: y
arg.summary: y coordinate in the parent surface local coordinate system

request.name: place_above
request.description:
Places this sub-surface just above the reference identified by sibling_token, changing the z-order. Z-order is double-buffered on the parent surface. A new sub-surface is initially added at the top.
Valid sibling_token values:
- The surface_token of the parent exported surface.
- The surface_token of any sibling cross-process sub-surface under the same parent, shared via out-of-band communication.
- An empty string (""), a sentinel meaning "place at the very top of the sibling stack".
If the sibling_token does not identify a valid target, the request is ignored and an invalid_sibling event is emitted.

arg.name: sibling_token
arg.summary: a surface_token or empty string for top

request.name: place_below
request.description: Places this sub-surface just below the reference identified by sibling_token. The same values are accepted as in place_above, except that the empty string sentinel is not valid and triggers an invalid_sibling event.

arg.name: sibling_token
arg.summary: a surface_token; empty string is not valid for place_below

event.name: invalid_sibling

description.summary: a place_above or place_below request could not be fulfilled

event.description: Emitted when a sibling_token does not identify a valid target. The corresponding restack request was ignored.
